analysis.title: FX Daily: Carry trade unwind in full swing
key_insights: Prospect of faster Fed tightening and dislocation in tech stocks is pulling funds into the dollar and the yen. Popular FX carry trades are being unwound across the board.

The S&P 500 is 8.5% off its highs of the year, versus a 9.5% correction in March this year and a 21% rout in March/April 2025. The trigger was the Fed's Christopher Waller putting a faster tightening cycle on the table last week.
Tech volatility may also reflect portfolio shuffling to participate in this week's $100bn Anthropic IPO.
ING sees a weak case for another 10% equity correction barring major earnings misses, since a Fed tightening driven by a demand shock is not necessarily bad for equities.

Next Wednesday's core PCE release for October is expected to show the year-on-year rate rising to 3.2% with upside risks, which would confirm the Fed needs to act. ING sees no reason for Fed rhetoric to soften soon.
ING expects the dollar to hold gains into next week and keeps 104.60 as the near-term DXY target.
Latam FX had a bad week. The Colombian peso, the most popular carry position, is off heavily. Brazil's $1bn FX intervention was quickly overwhelmed.

The South African rand is vulnerable after a big drop in metals. Crowded Hungarian forint positions are unwinding after a dovish National Bank of Hungary. Pressure may be building on long Turkish lira positions as implied yields rise.
Expectations are building for Reserve Bank of Australia rate cuts next year on the view that it has overtightened. ING flagged this as a key risk in its 2027 FX Outlook.
EUR/USD is consolidating below 1.10, held in a range by FX option barriers in the 1.0850-1.0950 area. ING sees continuing downside risk, with 1.0880 as the potential target.
Eurozone Q3 negotiated wages are expected at 2.6% y/y, well below the 4-5% seen in 2024-2025 that worried the ECB over second-round effects.
EUR/HUF above 373.65 (the April upside gap) would warn of an extension to 380. Long-end Hungarian local bonds are so far untouched, and a sharp yield spike there would signal a deeper correction.

UK PM Andy Burnham and EU leaders are expected to announce three agreements today: SPS (fewer border checks on food, animals and plants), ETS alignment, and a Youth Experience Scheme with up to 100,000 work visas for ages 18-31 for up to three years.

The EU-UK deals are fully expected and may not generate independent sterling strength. ING likes sterling over coming months because BoE tightening expectations should prove more resilient than the ECB's. EUR/GBP may stall near 0.8400, with a year-end forecast of 0.8300.

USD/BRL could extend to the 6.00/6.30 region as investors doubt Lula's commitment to fiscal consolidation. ING expects buyers of the real to reappear at those levels given high real rates. USD/MXN is trading through 19.00 after Banxico's November cut, with 19.60 the risk if the dollar stays strong.

Brazil's President Lula is seen as having no interest in fiscal consolidation.
